evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires differing nonzero manager PIDs and differing nonempty invocation IDs. It never verifies that both snapshots come from the same boot. If the guest reboots between the manager restart and the second inspect, the new boot can supply a different manager PID and invocation ID, so `manager_restarted` passes even though the intended command did not isolate a manager restart. The separate `boot_id_changed` check covers only the planned reboot snapshot pair, not this manager-restart interval. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair is a narrow correctness fix.
